resources.string: Encrypted vault in your git repo
Creates a new local vault. The Secret Key is shown once. There is no recovery if you lose it.
A vault is already on this device. Unlock it with the Master Password and Secret Key.
Use at least 10 characters for the Master Password.
Master Password entries do not match.
This account has no vaults yet
Write this down and store it offline. gitpass cannot show it again. The vault locks when you leave the app. This key stays on screen until you confirm that you saved it.
Copied. The clipboard clears in 60 seconds.

Account setup was interrupted before you confirmed saving the Secret Key, and gitpass never stores it. If you wrote it down, unlock with it. Otherwise this account cannot be opened; clear gitpass storage in Android Settings to start over.
Download and verify one encrypted snapshot into a separate local account. This is NOT two-way sync. Your current account is preserved. Imported data does not refresh automatically.

Select your own repository and branch. Use a dedicated fine-grained PAT restricted to this repository with Contents: read-only. The PAT stays in memory only and must be re-entered after lock or cancel.
First pull failed. Check repository, Contents permission, Master Password and Secret Key, and snapshot integrity. Existing accounts are preserved. Re-enter credentials to retry.
This vault exceeds the Android import KDF budget (8192–262144 KiB, iterations 1–6, lanes 1–4). No parameters were changed. Use a capable supported client; do not weaken your vault.

Local account selection is damaged. All account data was preserved, but account access is blocked to avoid selecting the wrong account. Do not uninstall or clear app data. Restore the non-secret account selection index before continuing.
